adr: ADR-152 D1 — one parts model: a bought part is described once, and a number lives in one place
what: The bought parts this package OWNS, one committed row per real part. Every row carries the identity block (id, name), the mass and price of one unit and a source line saying where those numbers came from, plus the per-domain block this package designs from: `propulsion` for a drone motor, `jointDrive` for an arm servo. parts-model.ts and servos.ts build DRONE_FITS[...].motor and STS3215_12V from these rows BY ID, so the drone's mass budget, its price and the arm's joint sizing all read this file. It is deliberately dependency-free JSON so another package that describes the same part — Circuit Lab's shaft-driver catalog — READS the row from the compiled copy (routes/engine/design/parts-catalog.json) as data, instead of restating its name, mass or price, and never imports this package's code. The `bought` list carries the hexapod's bought parts (ADR-202 spider-18): the identity block only, read by hexapod-design.ts by the ids SPIDER_18.boughtRowIds names, plus the die spring the latched-spring jump option takes.
notWhat: Not the parts a fit PICKS (quantity and the role a part plays in one fit belong to the fit in parts-model.ts), not a price quote and not a measurement of a unit in hand: a number marked typical is the class figure, replaced by the scale and the invoice at assembly.

units.approxUsd: approximate 2026 US street price of one unit, US dollars
units.propulsion.kv: motor velocity constant, rpm per volt, unloaded
units.jointDrive.secondsPer60: rated no-load time for 60 degrees of output travel, s
units.jointDrive.bodyMm: the case, length x width x height, mm
units.jointDrive.splineOffsetMm: case centre to the output axis along the length, mm. MEASURED on the servo in hand, not published in the vendor listings found: change it here before the pockets are printed
units.jointDrive.hornDiscMm: diameter of the disc horn supplied with the servo, mm. MEASURED on the servo in hand, not published: change it here before the hub recess is printed
units.bought: the identity block only: a part the hexapod design reads by id; the figures are class figures and approximate 2026 street prices, never a measurement

motors.name: 2306 brushless, 1700–1900 KV
motors.source: the 2306 class the recon-mini fit flies on a 6-inch prop at 4S, as the recon-drone hardware design sizes it (core docs/architecture/embodied-recon-drone-hardware.md, section 3: 1700–1900 KV on 4S, about 30 g each): 30 g is the class figure and 18 USD an approximate 2026 street price, not a measurement or a quote for a unit in hand; kv 1800 is the middle of the 1700–1900 KV class the design names

motors.name: 2807 brushless, 1300 KV
motors.source: the 2807 class the reserve recon-3d fit flies on a 7-inch prop at 6S: 45 g is the class figure and 28 USD an approximate 2026 street price, not a measurement or a quote for a unit in hand; kv 1300 is the rating the fit names

servos.name: Feetech STS3215 class serial-bus servo, 12 V, 1:345 metal gearbox
servos.source: rated figures and case: feetechrc.com STS3215 12 V product page (https://www.feetechrc.com/525603.html); continuous duty: robonine.com bench test (https://robonine.com/testing-of-feetech-sts3215-servomotor-backlash-repeatability-and-torque/) — stable at 15 kg·cm for 10 min, overload protection after a few cycles at 20 kg·cm, backlash about 0.87°

jointDrive.encoder: 12-bit magnetic (4096 steps per turn), 0–360° plus a multi-turn mode
